translation_en: Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to me: Malik narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said: The Prophet said, “Allah will say to the people of Paradise, ‘O people of Paradise!’ They will say, ‘At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure; all good is in Your hands.’ He will say, ‘Are you pleased?’ They will say, ‘Why would we not be pleased, our Lord, when You have given us what You have given no one else among Your creation?’ He will say, ‘Shall I not give you something better than that?’ They will say, ‘Our Lord, what could be better than that?’ He will say, ‘I bestow My pleasure upon you, and I will never be displeased with you after that.’”

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us: Fulayh narrated to us: Hilal narrated to us, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that one day the Prophet was speaking while a Bedouin was with him. He said, “A man among the people of Paradise will ask his Lord for permission to plant. He will say, ‘Are you not in whatever you wish?’ The man will say, ‘Yes, but I love to plant.’ He will sow quickly, and in the blink of an eye the plants will grow, stand upright, be harvested, and pile up like mountains. Allah Most High will say, ‘Here you are, son of Adam; nothing will satisfy you.’” The Bedouin said, “Messenger of Allah, you would find such a person only among Quraysh or the Ansar, for they are people of farming. We are not farmers.” The Messenger of Allah laughed.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, from Amr ibn Shurahbil, from Abdullah, who said: I asked the Prophet, “Which sin is greatest in Allah’s sight?” He said, “That you set up a rival to Allah when He created you.” I said, “That is indeed grave. Then which?” He said, “That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you.” I said, “Then which?” He said, “That you commit adultery with your neighbor’s wife.”

Al-Humaydi narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Mansur narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma‘mar, from Abdullah, who said: Two men from Thaqif and one Qurashi—or two Qurashis and one man from Thaqif—whose bellies were very fat and whose hearts had little understanding, gathered near the House. One said, “Do you think Allah hears what we say?” Another said, “He hears us if we speak aloud, but not if we speak quietly.” The other said, “If He hears us when we speak aloud, then He hears us when we speak quietly too.” Then Allah Most High revealed, “You did not conceal yourselves lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins testify against you…” Quran 41:22.

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Hatim ibn Wardan narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: “How can you ask the People of the Book about their scriptures when you have Allah’s Book with you, the most recent book from Allah? You read it pure, unmixed.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah informed me that Abdullah ibn Abbas said: “O community of Muslims, how can you ask the People of the Book about something when the Book Allah sent down to your Prophet is the most recent report from Allah, pure and unmixed? Allah has told you that the People of the Book altered what was in Allah’s Books and changed them, writing with their own hands and saying, ‘This is from Allah,’ in order to gain a small price. Does not the knowledge that has come to you prevent you from asking them? By Allah, we have never seen one of them ask you about what was sent down to you.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi Aishah, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning Allah’s words, “Do not move your tongue with it” Quran 75:16. He said: The Prophet found the revelation difficult and was moving his lips. Ibn Abbas said to me, “I will move them for you just as the Messenger of Allah used to move them.” Sa‘id said, “I will move them just as Ibn Abbas used to,” and he moved his lips. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed, “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. It is for Us to gather it and recite it” Quran 75:16–17. He said: Its gathering in your heart, then your reciting it. “When We recite it, follow its recitation” Quran 75:18. He said: Listen to it and be silent; then it is for Us to make you recite it. The Messenger of Allah, when Gabriel came to him, listened; when Gabriel departed, the Prophet recited it just as Gabriel had recited it to him.

Amr ibn Zurara narrated to me, from Hushaym: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning Allah’s words, “Do not recite your prayer aloud, nor recite it silently” Quran 17:110. He said: It was revealed while the Messenger of Allah was in hiding in Mecca. When he prayed with his companions, he raised his voice in reciting the Quran. When the polytheists heard him, they reviled the Quran, the One who sent it down, and the one who brought it. So Allah said to His Prophet, “Do not recite your prayer aloud”—meaning your recitation, lest the polytheists hear and revile the Quran—“nor recite it silently” so that your companions cannot hear you, “but seek a way between that.”

Ubayd ibn Ismail narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, who said: This verse, “Do not recite your prayer aloud, nor recite it silently” Quran 17:110, was revealed concerning supplication.

Ishaq narrated to us: Abu Asim narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Ibn Shihab informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “He is not one of us who does not recite the Quran melodiously.” Another narrator added, “and aloud.”

Qutaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “There is no envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah has given the Quran and who recites it during the night and during the day, and says, ‘If only I had been given what this man was given, I would do as he does’; and a man whom Allah has given wealth and who spends it rightly, and says, ‘If only I had been given what this man was given, I would do with it as he does.’”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: al-Zuhri said, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet, who said, “There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given the Quran and who recites it during the night and day, and a man whom Allah has given wealth and who spends it during the night and day.” I heard Sufyan say this several times; I did not hear him mention the report’s chain, though it is among his sound reports.

Al-Fadl ibn Ya‘qub narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Ja‘far al-Raqqi narrated to us: al-Mu‘tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Sa‘id ibn Ubaydullah al-Thaqafi narrated to us: Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani and Ziyad ibn Jubayr ibn Hayyah narrated to us, from Jubayr ibn Hayyah, who said: al-Mughirah said, “Our Prophet informed us of our Lord’s message: ‘Whoever among us is killed will go to Paradise.’”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ismail, from al-Sha‘bi, from Masruq, from Aishah, who said: Whoever tells you that Muhammad concealed anything—Muhammad said: Abu Amir al-Aqadi narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha‘bi, from Masruq, from Aishah, who said: “Whoever tells you that the Prophet concealed any revelation, do not believe him. Allah Most High says, ‘O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; if you do not, you have not conveyed His message’” Quran 5:67.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Wa’il, from Amr ibn Shurahbil, who said: Abdullah said: A man asked, “Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest in Allah’s sight?” He said, “That you call upon a rival alongside Allah when He created you.” He asked, “Then which?” He said, “That you kill your child for fear he will eat with you.” He asked, “Then which?” He said, “That you commit adultery with your neighbor’s wife.” Then Allah revealed confirming it: “Those who do not call upon another god alongside Allah, do not kill a soul whom Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery; whoever does that…” Quran 25:68.

Abdan informed us: Abdullah informed us: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri: Salim informed me, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said, “Your remaining time, compared with the nations who came before you, is like the time between the Asr prayer and sunset. The people of the Torah were given the Torah and acted by it until midday, then became unable, and were given one qirat each. The people of the Gospel were given the Gospel and acted by it until the Asr prayer, then became unable, and were given one qirat each. Then you were given the Quran and acted by it until sunset, and you were given two qirats each.” The People of the Book said, “These people did less work than us but received more reward.” Allah said, “Have I wronged you in any of your due?” They said, “No.” He said, “That is My favor; I give it to whom I will.”

Sulayman narrated to me: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from al-Walid. And Abbad ibn Ya‘qub al-Asadi informed us: Abbad ibn al-Awwam informed us, from al-Shaybani, from al-Walid ibn al-Ayzar, from Abu Amr al-Shaybani, from Ibn Mas‘ud, that a man asked the Prophet, “Which deeds are best?” He said, “Prayer at its proper time, kindness to parents, then striving in the cause of Allah.”

Abu al-Nu‘man narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from al-Hasan: Amr ibn Taghlib narrated to us, who said: Wealth came to the Prophet, and he gave some people and withheld it from others. He heard that they were displeased, so he said, “I give to one man and leave another, and the one I leave is dearer to me than the one I give to. I give to some people because of the anxiety and greed in their hearts, and I entrust other people to the richness and goodness Allah has placed in their hearts. Amr ibn Taghlib is among them.” Amr said, “I would not exchange the Messenger of Allah’s words for red camels.”

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to me: Abu Zayd, Sa‘id ibn al-Rabi al-Harawi, narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, who related from his Lord: “When the servant draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm’s length; when he draws near to Me by an arm’s length, I draw near to him by a fathom; and when he comes to Me walking, I come to him hastening.”

Musaddad narrated to us, from Yahya, from al-Taymi, from Anas ibn Malik, from Abu Hurayrah, who said—sometimes he mentioned the Prophet—“When the servant draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm’s length; and when he draws near to Me by an arm’s length, I draw near to him by a fathom or a cubit.” Mu‘tamir said: I heard my father say: I heard Anas narrate, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who related it from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

Adam narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us: I heard Abu Hurayrah narrate from the Prophet, who related from your Lord: “Every deed has an expiation, and fasting is for Me, and I reward it. The smell from the mouth of the fasting person is more pleasant to Allah than the fragrance of musk.”

Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us. Khalifah said to me: Yazid ibn Zuray informed us, from Sa‘id, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet, in what he related from his Lord, who said, “It is not fitting for a servant to say that he is better than Yunus ibn Matta.” He traced his lineage to his father.

Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj informed us: Shababah narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Muawiyah ibn Qurrah, from Abdullah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, who said: On the day of the Conquest, I saw the Messenger of Allah on his she-camel reciting Surat al-Fath, or part of Surat al-Fath, in a wavering, melodic manner. Muawiyah recited in imitation of Ibn Mughaffal’s recitation and said, “Were it not that people would gather around you, I would recite in the same wavering manner as Ibn Mughaffal.” He was imitating the Prophet. I asked Muawiyah, “How did he modulate it?” He said, “Aa, aa, aa,” three times.

Ibn Abbas said: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb informed me that Heraclius called his translator, then asked for the letter of the Prophet. He read it: “In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. From Muhammad, servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, and: ‘O People of the Book, come to a word common between us and you…’” the verse.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us: Ali ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah said, “Do not affirm the People of the Book, nor deny them, but say, ‘We believe in Allah and what has been sent down…’” the verse Quran 2:136.

Musaddad narrated to us: Ismail narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, who said: A Jewish man and woman who had committed adultery were brought to the Prophet. He asked the Jews, “What do you do with them?” They said, “We blacken their faces and disgrace them.” He said, “Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful” Quran 3:93. They came and asked a man whom they trusted, “O one-eyed man, recite.” He recited until he reached a passage and placed his hand over it. The Prophet said, “Raise your hand.” He raised it, and there was the verse of stoning plainly visible. The man said, “Muhammad, stoning is prescribed for them, but we conceal it among ourselves.” The Prophet ordered that they be stoned, and they were. I saw him bend over her to shield her from the stones.

Ibrahim ibn Hamzah narrated to me: Ibn Abi Hazim narrated to me, from Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who heard the Prophet say, “Allah has not listened to anything as He listens to a Prophet with a beautiful voice reciting the Quran aloud.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah informed me about the account of Aishah concerning what the people of the slander said about her. Each narrated to me part of the account. She said: I lay down on my bed. At that time I knew I was innocent and that Allah would declare me innocent, but by Allah I did not think that Allah would send down recited revelation concerning me. I considered my own situation too insignificant for Allah to speak about me in a matter that would be recited. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed, “Indeed, those who brought the slander…” all ten verses Quran 24:11.

Abu Nu‘aym narrated to us: Mis‘ar narrated to us, from Adi ibn Thabit—I think from al-Bara—who said: I heard the Prophet recite during the night prayer, “By the fig and the olive” Quran 95:1. I never heard anyone with a better voice or recitation than him.

Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet was concealed in Mecca and used to raise his voice. When the polytheists heard him, they reviled the Quran and the one who brought it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet, “Do not recite your prayer aloud, nor recite it silently” Quran 17:110.
